Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. I went and found five digital products that have each sold over a thousand copies, so you don't have to. They're all on screen so you can go and check the numbers for yourself. Number four is the one nobody expected, including me, so stay for that one. Number one is a brush set at $5 and it's done 23,500 sales. It's not a course, it's not a bundle, it's just brushes. Number two is a travel planner built inside Notion at $20, and that's done over 2,900 sales. There are nearly 20,000 Notion templates on that platform, and it beat all of them because it's about travelling and not about productivity. Number three is a teaching resource at $25 with 2,900 sales, and it was obviously made for teachers by somebody who used to be a teacher — nobody else would have known exactly how to build it that way. Number four is the one I did not expect: a drawing course at $100 with 1,800 sales. A hundred dollars, for foundations in drawing with brushes and charcoal. Nearly 2,000 people have paid for it. That's insane. And number five is a freelance dashboard at $97 with 1,200 sales. Now look at what's in that list. There's no AI in it anywhere. No make money online, no productivity system. It's brushes, travel, teaching, drawing and freelancing — and every one of them is a specific person doing a specific thing. The prices run from $5 all the way up to $100. So there isn't one right price, just the right price for the person you pick. Stop asking what sells and start asking who you actually know something about, because that's the only thing these five have in common.
